Beyond the Race · Hatipoti Tea Estate

Folktea Festival

A slow weekend among the tea bushes

We open our Tea Garden house and grounds to a small number of guests at a time — camping under the estate sky, waking up to views of Mt. Gorichen, spending mornings plucking tea, fishing, and enjoying Assamese meals cooked the way we cook them at home.

Close enough to Kaziranga’s Northern Range for a day in the wild, and to Nohmora near the Assam–Arunachal border for a quiet river picnic. The Brahmaputra at Biswanath Ghat is there to explore — yet Hatipoti stays quiet enough to do absolutely nothing.

Days move slowly: a morning round of tea plucking, a cooking session at the bagan house, an afternoon picnic by the river, and evenings of BBQ, bonfires and stargazing. During Folktea Festival weekend there’s a little more — folk music, tea and evenings by the fire, woven into the stay rather than being the whole point of it.

Garden open 28 – 30 November

Come for the tea gardens. Stay for the slower pace of Assam.
